design_principles: Open-ended, neutral-stem prompts inviting multi-step reasoning without priming RT (no 'step by step', no 'carefully', no 'show your work'). Mix of 'work out why', 'explain', 'compare', 'predict'. Target response length: 150-300 words.

prompts.text: Work out why a mug of coffee cools faster than a pot of the same liquid.
Compare what happens to a ball thrown vertically on the Moon vs on Earth.
Predict what you'd see if the sun suddenly had half its current mass.
Reason through why a high-calorie diet doesn't always cause weight gain.
Explain how natural selection could produce something as precise as the vertebrate eye.
Compare two hypotheses for why aging exists.
Walk through what might be wrong with a patient with chest pain and shortness of breath.
Explain why the same drug dose can be safe in one person and toxic in another.
Compare the tradeoffs of screening for a disease vs waiting for symptoms.
Work out whether cutting taxes raises or lowers government revenue.
Explain why two cities with the same average income can have very different living standards.
Predict what happens to local businesses when a large online retailer opens a warehouse nearby.
Reason through why group brainstorming often produces worse ideas than individual thinking.
Explain why people remember emotionally charged events better than mundane ones.
Compare two explanations for why anxiety runs in families.
Work out why ice cubes float while most solid forms of substances sink in their liquids.
Explain why adding salt lowers water's freezing point.
Compare two possible reasons a previously-reliable reaction starts giving low yields.
Reason through why bridges built in the 1950s need different retrofits than ones built in the 1980s.
Explain how engineers decide between redundant systems and inspection-based maintenance.
Work out why a battery pack that tests well can still fail in service.
Reason through why a glacier melts even when average temperatures don't rise.
Explain why tsunamis are barely noticeable in deep ocean but destructive near shore.
Compare what you'd expect from slow vs fast sea-level rise.
